topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the cancer lecture series, and presents the learning objectives focused on cancer causes, environmental exposures, and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer Causation: Genetic Evolution, Intrinsic Risk, and Environmental Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer development, debating the relative contributions of intrinsic random mutations versus environmental exposures and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Specific Carcinogens: Pathogens, Radiation, and Chemically Activated Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail various environmental and biological agents—including infectious pathogens, dietary toxins, UV radiation, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons—and their mechanisms of damaging DNA.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, contrasting tumor initiators with promoters and exploring how chronic inflammation, cellular signaling, and host developmental stages permit tumor growth.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the experimental, genomic, toxicological, and epidemiological methodologies used to identify mutational signatures and determine whether specific agents are carcinogenic.
